1.
Heard Sri Munna Tiwari, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Jai Kishan Chaurasiya, learned State Law Officer and perused the record.
2. As informed by learned State Law Officer, notice to the informant has been served on 29.07.2024 but none is present on behalf of the informant.
3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 325 of 2023, under Sections 363, 376, 343 I.P.C. and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act, Police Station Pataherwa, District Kushi Nagar, during the pendency of trial.

sentences.text: The FIR was instituted by the informant against unknown person of having enticed away his minor daughter aged about 15 years on 16.11.2023 at about 6 a.m.
ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT :
5. The applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case and he has nothing to do with the said offence.
6. The FIR is delayed by about more than one day and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.

7. The victim seems to be a consenting party as is but evident from her statement recorded u/s 164 Cr.P.C. whereby she has stated that the applicant met the victim on the way and caught hold of her hand, as such her brother started beating him on 16.11.2023 at about 10:00 p.m to 11:00 p.m. but the applicant had taken her forcibly to his house and kept her during the night.
In the next morning at about 6 p.m., he is stated to have taken her on a motorcycle to some unknown village and committed rape with her and kept her there for about two months.
8. She has also stated that subsequently he was taking her somewhere else on 16.11.2023 on a motorcycle, as such she somehow escaped from his clutches.
It cannot be believed.

9. The victim by her looks seems to be major and just to make fall within the parameters of POCSO Act, a transfer certificate of class-VIIIth has been made subsequently indicating her date of birth to be 01.01.2008.
The said document is not admissible in the light of Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 10. The instant case is a counter blast to the FIR No.307 of 2023 which was instituted against the informant and other family members regarding having assaulted the applicant, causing grievous injuries to him on 17.11.2023 at about 9-10 p.m.
The applicant had sustained head injury in the said case.
11. The medical report does not corroborate the prosecution story.
12. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
13. There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 23.06.2024.
The applicant is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail

,
he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF STATE :
14. The bail application has been opposed but the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant could not be disputed.

sentences.text: CONCLUSION:
15. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

16. A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
17.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasised that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that "bail is a rule and jail is an exception".
18.
Learned State Law Officer could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
19. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned State Law Officer.

20. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, and taking into consideration the delay in FIR and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

21. Let the applicant- Vipin Gaud involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.

23 . It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
